subject: dsa
title: Target Sum
summary: Choosing plus or minus signs to hit a target becomes a subset-sum count. The subset of numbers marked plus must sum to (total + target) / 2, so dp counts subsets reaching that value: keep the count without the number, then add the count that uses it.
problem: Count the sign assignments to nums = [1, 1, 2] that sum to target = 0. With total 4 this needs a plus-subset summing to (4 + 0) / 2 = 2. Rows are the numbers added so far (none, +1, +1, +2); columns are sums 0 through 2. dp[i][s] = dp[i-1][s] + dp[i-1][s - num].

steps.caption: Count subsets summing to 2, which is (total 4 plus target 0) / 2. Columns are sums 0 through 2, and with no numbers there is one way to make 0.
Add the first 1. Sum 0 keeps its one way, and sum 1 now has one way by taking this number.
Add the second 1. Sum 1 reaches two ways and sum 2 reaches one way by combining both 1s.
Add the 2. Sum 2 now also counts the lone 2, lifting it to two ways.
The cell at sum 2 is 2, so there are 2 valid sign assignments.
